gemini-2.5-flash.standardized_narrative: Syndicate 1110 experienced a net prior year reserve release of GBP 1.3 million in 2014, representing a 1.80% release of its opening gross claims outstanding. This was primarily driven by a GBP 2.0 million surplus on direct business, specifically from the Property line of business. This favourable development was partly offset by a GBP 0.7 million deficit on reinsurance accepted business, which arose from a deterioration in the Casualty book, although this was partly mitigated by a surplus on the reinsurance Property book. The 2012 year of account had been impacted by large claims including a mining landslide, a contractor's liability claim, and power claims, while the 2013 year of account included a significant Canadian construction loss.

gpt-5-mini.exact_reserve_text: A surplus run-off deviation of GBP 1.3 million was experienced in 2014 (2013: GBP 6.4 million surplus). This was made up of a surplus on the prior year claims provisions of GBP 2.0 million on direct business (2013: GBP 3.4 million surplus) and a GBP 0.7 million deficit on reinsurance accepted business (2013: GBP 3.0 million surplus). The direct improvements primarily arose from the fire and other damage to property books and the reinsurance accepted deteriorations primarily arose from a deterioration on the casualty book although this was partly offset by a surplus on the property book (2013: the direct and reinsurance accepted surpluses primarily arose from the fire and other damage to property books).
gpt-5-mini.standardized_narrative: The syndicate experienced a small prior-year surplus (run-off) of GBP 1.3m in 2014, comprised of a GBP 2.0m release on direct business mainly driven by favourable development on property (fire and other damage to property) and a GBP 0.7m adverse movement on reinsurance accepted business driven by deterioration on the casualty book. Overall this resulted in a net prior-year release of c.1.8% of opening gross claims reserves.
